cards.text: Saul, Israel's king, is dead. David, whom Samuel the prophet anointed to be king (1 Samuel 16:1, 13), is back from the slaughter of the Amalekites and has been in Ziklag two days. On the third day, a man arrives from Saul's camp with torn clothes and dust on his head.

cards.question: When the man from Saul's camp reaches David, he falls to the ground to pay him homage.

cards.text: David asks where he's coming from, and the man says he escaped from the Israelite camp. Then David asks, "What was the outcome?" and I bet his heart is POUNDING.

cards.question: The man tells David that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead. What does he say the troops did?

cards.text: David doesn't just take his word for it. He asks the young man how he KNOWS Saul and Jonathan are dead.
The man says he "happened to be on Mount Gilboa," and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and the cavalry closing in. He says Saul turned, saw him and called out to him.

cards.question: The man says Saul asked him who he was. What does the man say he told Saul?
The man says Saul begged him to stand over him and kill him, because ___ had seized him.

cards.text: The man says he stood over Saul and killed him, because he knew that after Saul had fallen he couldn't survive. Then he says he took something off Saul to bring to David.

cards.question: The man says he took two things from Saul and brought them to David. What are they?
When David hears the news and tears his clothes, all the men with him do the same.
David and his men mourn and weep and fast until evening, but only for Saul and Jonathan.

cards.text: Then David asks the young man where he's from, and he says, "I am the son of a foreigner," an Amalekite.

cards.question: David has a question for the Amalekite who says he killed Saul. What does David ask him?

answers.text: Why he wasn't afraid to kill God's chosen king
Why he didn't bring Jonathan's body back home
Why he left the battle before it was over

cards.question: Then David summons one of his young men and tells him to ___ the Amalekite.

cards.text: The young man strikes him down, and he dies. David had already told him, "Your blood be on your own head because your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I killed the LORD’s anointed.’"
Then David takes up a lament for Saul and his son Jonathan. And he gives an order about it.

cards.question: David orders that his lament for Saul and Jonathan, the Song of the Bow, be taught. Who is supposed to learn it?

cards.text: The song is written in the Book of Jashar, and it opens with Israel's glory lying slain on the heights. Then comes a line David keeps coming back to: "How the mighty have fallen!"
Next David names two Philistine cities. He says, "Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon," and then he gives his reason.

cards.question: Why doesn't David want the news of Saul's death told in Gath and Ashkelon?

answers.text: So no one comes after Judah
So Israel can hear it first

cards.text: Then David speaks to the mountains of Gilboa: may they have no dew or rain, no fields yielding offerings of grain.

cards.question: David speaks against the mountains of Gilboa because that is where the shield of Saul was defiled.

cards.text: Then David remembers Saul and Jonathan in battle. He sings that the bow of Jonathan did not retreat.

cards.question: In David's song, the sword of Saul returned empty.
David calls Saul and Jonathan beloved and delightful in life. What does he say about them in death?

cards.text: David says they were swifter than eagles and stronger than lions. And this is the same Saul who searched for David every day (1 Samuel 23:14).

cards.question: Why does David say the daughters of Israel should weep for Saul?

answers.text: He dressed them in scarlet and gold
He gave them homes in the hills
He sang songs in their honor

cards.text: David comes back to that line: "How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle!" Then he turns to Jonathan, Saul's son, lying slain on the heights.

cards.question: Speaking straight to Jonathan, David grieves for him and calls him my ___.
David says Jonathan's love to him was extraordinary.

cards.text: David closes with that line one more time: "How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!" The song is over, friend, but this story's not done.
